## NL2319

The message of an error contains:

```text
…` under a type constructor instead of passing it on, so the chain has no end; name `…
```

[`nl2319_generic_expanding_field.ts`](https://github.com/amritk/nish/blob/main/tests/wordings/nl2319_generic_expanding_field.ts):

```ts
// NL2319: the struct half of the termination rule (WP18 §4). A field whose
// type puts the class's own type argument under a constructor asks for a
// strictly larger instantiation, so the chain has no end, and the sentence
// names the two shapes that do terminate rather than a depth — the fix is to
// change the annotation, not to raise a limit.
//
// `tests/cases/reject_generic_expanding_field` already pins these words. What
// this corpus adds is the *code*: `tests/diagnostic_coverage.js` reads the
// `--json` object and fails if the message comes out NL0000, or under a
// number other than the one the registry froze, which is what a reword would
// do to it.
class Nest<T> {
  inner: Nest<T[]> | null;
  constructor() {
    this.inner = null;
  }
}

export const main = (): i32 => {
  const n = new Nest<i32>();
  return n.inner === null ? 0 : 1;
};
```

```text
Monomorphising `Nest` would not terminate: `Nest<i32>` names `Nest<i32[]>`, which puts `i32` under a type constructor instead of passing it on, so the chain has no end; name `T` itself, or a type that does not mention it
```


## NL2352

The message of an error contains:

```text
…` releases what a body allocates after every element: a parallel body may allocate only temporaries it drops before it returns, and this analysis stops following a value once it is stored…
```

[`nl2352_field_store.ts`](https://github.com/amritk/nish/blob/main/tests/wordings/nl2352_field_store.ts):

```ts
// NL2352: a string a parallel body builds and stores into a field of an
// element is refused, with the serial loop that does the store on the calling thread.
import { parallelMap } from "nish/threads";

class Row {
  n: i32;
  label: string;

  constructor(n: i32) {
    this.n = n;
    this.label = "";
  }
}

export const main = (): i32 => {
  const rows: Row[] = [new Row(1), new Row(2)];
  const ys = parallelMap(rows, (r: Row): i32 => {
    r.label = `row ${r.n}`;
    return r.n;
  });
  console.log(ys.length);
  console.log(rows[1].label);
  return 0;
};
```

```text
`(r) => ...` allocates at tests/wordings/nl2352_field_store.ts:18:15 and stores the allocation into memory, and `parallelMap` releases what a body allocates after every element: a parallel body may allocate only temporaries it drops before it returns, and this analysis stops following a value once it is stored; make it answer what it allocates and do the store after the call, or run it on the thread that called it, `` const ys: i32[] = []; for (const r of rows) { r.label = `row ${r.n}`; ys.push(r.n) } ``
```

[`nl2352_push_captured.ts`](https://github.com/amritk/nish/blob/main/tests/wordings/nl2352_push_captured.ts):

```ts
// NL2352: a parallel body that stores what it allocates into an array its
// caller owns is refused, and the remedy is the serial loop in the program's names.
import { parallelMap } from "nish/threads";

export const main = (): i32 => {
  const xs: i32[] = [1, 2, 3];
  const seen: string[] = [];
  const ys = parallelMap(xs, (x: i32): i32 => {
    seen.push(`${x}`);
    return x * 2;
  });
  console.log(ys.length);
  console.log(seen.length);
  return 0;
};
```

```text
`(x) => ...` allocates at tests/wordings/nl2352_push_captured.ts:9:15 and stores the allocation into memory, and `parallelMap` releases what a body allocates after every element: a parallel body may allocate only temporaries it drops before it returns, and this analysis stops following a value once it is stored; make it answer what it allocates and do the store after the call, or run it on the thread that called it, `` const ys: i32[] = []; for (const x of xs) { seen.push(`${x}`); ys.push(x * 2) } ``
```

## NL2394

The message of an error contains:

```text
…: a scope's tasks run, and store their answers, when its block ends, and under Node each runs and stores where it is spawned, so a destination is a fresh `const` array that is never handed on, and between a scope's first `spawn` and the end of its block its thread neither reads a destination nor writes memory a task may read
```

[`nl2394_thread_region_read.ts`](https://github.com/amritk/nish/blob/main/tests/wordings/nl2394_thread_region_read.ts):

```ts
// NL2394: Between a scope's first `spawn` and the end of its block, its thread may not
// read an array a task stores into: natively `sums[0]` is still 0 here, and
// under Node the task has already stored 6.
import { scope } from "nish/threads";

const sumOf = (xs: i32[]): i32 => {
  let t: i32 = 0;
  for (const x of xs) {
    t = t + x;
  }
  return t;
};

export const main = (): i32 => {
  const xs: i32[] = [1, 2, 3];
  const sums: i32[] = [0];
  {
    using s = scope();
    s.spawn(sumOf, xs, sums, 0);
    console.log(`${sums[0]}`);
  }
  return sums[0];
};
```

```text
This reads `sums`, a destination of a task of `s`, before the scope joins: a scope's tasks run, and store their answers, when its block ends, and under Node each runs and stores where it is spawned, so a destination is a fresh `const` array that is never handed on, and between a scope's first `spawn` and the end of its block its thread neither reads a destination nor writes memory a task may read
```

## NL2462

The message of an error contains:

```text
…finding, because the arena memory it describes stays allocated after nothing in the program can reach it any more…
```

[`nl2462_deny_retention.ts`](https://github.com/amritk/nish/blob/main/tests/wordings/nl2462_deny_retention.ts) (compiled with `--deny-retention`):

```ts
// NL2462: under --deny-retention, an arena-retention warning in the program's
// own code is an error that keeps the warning's code and text.
export const lastLine = (rows: i32): i32 => {
  let last = "";
  for (let i = 0; i < rows; i++) {
    last = `row ${i}`;
  }
  return last.length;
};
```

```text
`--deny-retention` refuses this NL9016 finding, because the arena memory it describes stays allocated after nothing in the program can reach it any more: `last` is given a new allocation on every pass of this loop and drops the one the pass before gave it: nothing can reach that value again and nothing frees it while the loop runs, so memory grows with every pass. Declare `last` with `const` inside the loop when only its pass reads it, or keep what the last pass needs as numbers and build the value once after the loop
```

## NL2470

The message of an error contains:


```ts
// NL2470: one lock is held at a time. A second `lock()` inside a guard's block is
// how two tasks taking the same two locks in opposite orders deadlock.
import { Mutex } from "nish/threads";

class Counter {
  n: i32 = 0;
}

export const main = (): i32 => {
  const a = new Mutex<Counter>(new Counter());
  const b = new Mutex<Counter>(new Counter());

    using ga = a.lock();
    using gb = b.lock();
    ga.value.n = gb.value.n;
  }
  return 0;
};
```

```ts
// NL2471: a task writes shared memory only through a guard. `hits` is the parent's
// array, written here without a lock while the other task writes it too.

class Counter {
  n: i32 = 0;
}

class Job {
  total: Mutex<Counter>;
  hits: i32[];
  constructor(total: Mutex<Counter>, hits: i32[]) {
    this.total = total;
    this.hits = hits;
  }
}

const count = (job: Job): i32 => {
  {
    using g = job.total.lock();
    g.value.n = g.value.n + 1;
  }
  job.hits[0] = job.hits[0] + 1;
  return 0;
};

export const main = (): i32 => {
  const total = new Mutex<Counter>(new Counter());
  const hits: i32[] = [0];
  const done: i32[] = [0, 0];
  {
    using s = scope();
    s.spawn(count, new Job(total, hits), done, 0);
    s.spawn(count, new Job(total, hits), done, 1);
  }
  return hits[0];
};
```

```text
`count` writes memory its caller can see at tests/wordings/nl2471_mutex_task_unguarded.ts:23:3, and `spawn` runs it beside the scope's other tasks: make scratch only this task uses inside it, because an object handed in as the argument is shared memory even when the `spawn` made it, since where an argument was made is not tracked.     s.spawn(count, new Job(ch, tally), out, 0);
```
```ts
  }
  return out[0];
};
```

```text
A loop over a channel is reached while `g` holds its lock: a receive waits, and nothing waits while a lock is held, so there is no receive inside a guard's block, directly or through any function it calls (a `send` never waits, and may stay)
```

## NL2483

The message of an error contains:

```text
…: no task both sends and receives on one channel, because a channel closes only once every task that may send on it has returned, and this one would wait in its own loop for its own return…
```

[`nl2483_channel_send_and_receive.ts`](https://github.com/amritk/nish/blob/main/tests/wordings/nl2483_channel_send_and_receive.ts):

```ts
// NL2483, C6: no task both sends and receives on one channel: it would wait for its
// own sends to close the channel, which they do only when it returns.
import { Channel, scope } from "nish/threads";

class Pipe {
  ch: Channel<i32>;
  n: i32;

  constructor(ch: Channel<i32>, n: i32) {
    this.ch = ch;
    this.n = n;
  }
}

const produce = (p: Pipe): i32 => {
  for (let i: i32 = 1; i <= p.n; i++) {
    p.ch.send(i);
  }
  return p.n;
};

const consume = (p: Pipe): i32 => {
  let sum: i32 = 0;
  for (const x of p.ch) {
    sum = sum + x;
  }
  return sum;
};

const echo = (p: Pipe): i32 => {
  p.ch.send(1);
  let sum: i32 = 0;
  for (const x of p.ch) {
    sum = sum + x;
  }
  return sum;
};

export const main = (): i32 => {
  const out: i32[] = [0];
  const ch = new Channel<i32>();
  {
    using s = scope();
    s.spawn(echo, new Pipe(ch, 0), out, 0);
  }
  return out[0];
};
```

```text
`echo` may both send and receive on `ch`: no task both sends and receives on one channel, because a channel closes only once every task that may send on it has returned, and this one would wait in its own loop for its own return; split it into a task that sends and a task that receives, or answer the result through a second channel
```

The message of an error contains:

```ts
// NL2484, C2: a channel is used only in a top-level function's own body, never inside an
// arrow: an arrow is lifted into a function of its own, which the channel rules
// do not follow, so a channel there would escape every one of them.
import { Channel, scope } from "nish/threads";

class Pipe {
  ch: Channel<i32>;

  constructor(ch: Channel<i32>) {
    this.ch = ch;
  }
}

const apply = <T>(x: T, f: (x: T) => i32): i32 => f(x);

const relay = (p: Pipe): i32 =>
  apply(p, (q: Pipe): i32 => {
    q.ch.send(1);
    return 1;
  });

export const main = (): i32 => {
  const out: i32[] = [0];
  const ch = new Channel<i32>();
  {
    using s = scope();
    s.spawn(relay, new Pipe(ch), out, 0);
  }
  let sum: i32 = 0;
  for (const x of ch) {
    sum = sum + x;
  }
  return sum + out[0];
};
```

```ts
// NL2510: a task's arrow captures a value that reaches a `Mutex` deeper than
// a field of its own class.
import { Mutex, scope } from "nish/threads";

class Tally {
  total: i32 = 0;
}

class Inner {
  m: Mutex<Tally>;

  constructor(m: Mutex<Tally>) {
    this.m = m;
  }
}

class Outer {
  inner: Inner;

  constructor(inner: Inner) {
    this.inner = inner;
  }
}

const bump = (o: Outer): void => {
  using g = o.inner.m.lock();
  g.value.total = g.value.total + 1;
};

export const main = (): i32 => {
  const o = new Outer(new Inner(new Mutex<Tally>(new Tally())));
  {
    using s = scope();
    s.spawn(() => bump(o));
  }
  return 0;
};
```

```text
The task's arrow reads `o`, which is `Outer` and reaches a `Mutex` through `o.inner.m`: a captured value is the task's argument, and a `Mutex` reaches a task as an argument or as a field of the class an argument is, never deeper, so which tasks share a lock is a question the checker can answer
```

```ts
// NL2529: a write through the union.
enum Kind {
  Circle,
  Square,
  Tri,
}

  readonly kind: Kind.Circle = Kind.Circle;
  r: i32 = 1;
}

class Square {
  readonly kind: Kind.Square = Kind.Square;
  side: i32 = 2;
  x: i32 = 0;
}

type Shape = Circle | Square;

const pick = (n: i32): Shape => (n > 0 ? new Circle() : new Square());

class Spot {

}

};
```

```text
Cannot assign to `x` through the union `Square | Spot`: a union is read-only, so assign to the variant itself
```

```ts
  side: i32;
```

```ts
    this.side = side;
  }

  readonly kind: Kind.Tri;
  base: i32;
}

type Shape = Circle | Square | Tri;

const pick = (n: i32): Shape => {
  if (n % 3 === 0) {
    return new Circle(n);
  }
  if (n % 3 === 1) {

};

    return 2;
  }
  if (s.kind === Kind.Tri) {

  }

};
```

## NL2689

The message of an error contains:

```text
…what a task hands on may be memory of its own region, freed while the task it spawned still holds it
```

[`nl2689_task_nested_spawn.ts`](https://github.com/amritk/nish/blob/main/tests/wordings/nl2689_task_nested_spawn.ts):

```ts
// NL2689: a spawned task may not itself spawn a task with an object or an
// array: what it hands on may be memory of its own region, which is freed when
// it ends while the task it spawned still holds it.
import { sleep, spawn } from "nish:async"

class Box {
  n: i32 = 0
}

async function inner(box: Box): Promise<void> {
  await sleep(1)
  console.log(`${box.n}`)
}

async function outer(n: i32): Promise<void> {
  const box = new Box()
  box.n = n
  spawn(inner(box))
}

export async function main(): Promise<i32> {
  spawn(outer(3))
  return 0
}
```

```text
`outer` runs as a spawned task, in a region of its own that is freed when it ends, and spawns a task with an object or an array, itself or through a callee: what a task hands on may be memory of its own region, freed while the task it spawned still holds it
```

## NL2690

The message of an error contains:

```text
…a spawned task takes a function argument only when it captures nothing…
```

[`nl2690_spawn_capture.ts`](https://github.com/amritk/nish/blob/main/tests/wordings/nl2690_spawn_capture.ts):

```ts
// NL2690: a spawned task takes a function argument only when it captures
// nothing. The arrow reads `base` of `start`, a value that would ride in the
// task's frame where neither the spawn's argument rule nor the task's region
// rules see it.
import { sleep, spawn } from "nish:async"

async function later(f: (n: i32) => i32, n: i32): Promise<void> {
  await sleep(1)
  console.log(`${f(n)}`)
}

async function start(base: i32): Promise<void> {
  spawn(later((n: i32): i32 => n + base, 2))
}

export async function main(): Promise<i32> {
  await start(40)
  return 0
}
```

```text
`spawn` hands `later<(n) => ...>` an arrow that reads `base` of the function it is written in: a spawned task takes a function argument only when it captures nothing, because the task may run after that function returns; pass the value to the task as an argument of its own, or hand it a top-level function
```
